q-74094.name: Question 1
q-74094.problem: Given that $‖v‖=6$ and $u\cdot v=-9$, find the smallest possible value of $‖u‖.$
q-74094.worked_solution:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have   

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-9| & \le ‖u‖\cdot 6 \\ 9 & \le 6\cdot ‖u‖ \\ 3 & \le 2\cdot ‖u‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $\frac{1}{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3 & \le \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot ‖u‖ \\ \frac{3}{2} & \le ‖u‖\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖u‖$
is  $\frac{3}{2}.$

q-40196.name: Question 3
q-40196.problem: Consider the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{k} \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u\cdot v=-2$ and $‖v‖=1$, what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
q-40196.worked_solution:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

$$
|u\cdot v|\le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖.
$$

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $‖u‖.$ So first, we compute $‖u‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{k})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2+k}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-2| & \le \sqrt{2+k}\cdot (1) \\ 2 & \le \sqrt{2+k} \\ {2}^{2} & \le (\sqrt{2+k})^{2} \\ 4 & \le 2+k \\ 2 & \le k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $2.$

q-74133.problem: Let $A(1,2,3,-1)$, $B(0,1,2,0)$, and $C(1,1,3,0).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
q-74133.worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
